brief.headline: Aluminium hit an eight-month intraday low of $3,023 on Monday before recovering to about $3,058 three-month (Reuters), as a strong dollar, easing Gulf supply fears and Citi's call for a 2027 surplus weigh - the July floor is now being tested on an official basis, while Hormuz tanker attacks keep energy and freight costs high.
bullets: WHAT MOVED: Reuters reports three-month aluminium at $3,058 in Monday's official open-outcry (+0.3%) after touching $3,023, the lowest since 13-February; prices are down 19% from June's four-year high. This page's board stays on the verified Friday 09-October official (cash $3,055.50, three-month $3,070.00, $14.50 contango, stock 238,875 t) because Monday's full official could not be verified this run.

WHY: the dollar index near 102.5, its highest since April 2025, ahead of US inflation data; easing Gulf supply concerns and expected Indonesian capacity; Citi sees a 1.8 Mt surplus in 2027 versus a 941,000 t deficit this year. Low visible inventories are still cited as support.

ENERGY AND LOGISTICS: two more tankers were attacked near Hormuz on Sunday (one Suezmax set on fire, two sailors missing); Brent traded above $103-105 and European gas hit its highest since December 2022 at about 84 EUR/MWh - raising smelter power-cost risk in Europe.

WHAT TO WATCH: whether a verified official settles beneath 3,061.5 (opens $2,980-3,000); US inflation data this week; Alcoa's Q3 results on Thursday 15-October after the New York close; and the mid-October carbon settlements around 17-18 October.

On the Friday 09-October official cash settled $3,055.50, down $5.00 or -0.16%, and three-month $3,070.00, up $1.00 or 0.03% - $8.50 above the 3,061.5 July low but $7.00 beneath the 3,077 weekly 50% retracement on the weekly close. Aluminium lagged a broad base-metal rebound: zinc +1.19%, copper +1.06%, nickel +0.77% and lead +0.51% in three-month terms. drivers.text: The Q4 Japanese premium has settled 35% lower, at $255/t — SETTLED: Reuters (07-October) reported that some Japanese buyers agreed to pay $255/t over LME cash for October-December shipments, down 35% from $395/t in Q3 and below producers' initial offers of $310-325/t; producers named in the talks included Rio Tinto and South32, and talks with other buyers were ongoing. A Japanese trading-house source cited recovering Middle East output after the March attacks on Gulf smelters and rising Indonesian shipments. Negotiations ran longer than usual because of a wide gap between the two sides. The settlement sits inside the $245-260/t offer range AL Circle reported on 06-October, and above CRU's $202/t Asia CIF assessment. WHY IT MATTERS: the quarterly MJP is the reference for much Asian physical business, so the regional premium level resets about $140/t lower for the quarter.
drivers.source: Reuters via LSE.co.uk - Some Japanese aluminium buyers agree to pay Q4 premiums of $255/t, 35% lower than Q3 (07-Oct-2026)

drivers.text: Spot premiums have fallen below the new quarterly benchmark - but sellers' pressure is easing — SMM's 09-October assessment puts CIF Japan MJP spot at $230/t, $25 beneath the $255/t Q4 quarterly settlement, with Korea at $216-223/t and Thailand at $249/t. SMM concludes the outlook for overseas premiums 'has become less bearish' and premiums may stabilise or recover modestly near term, but a stronger rebound needs clearer improvement in downstream orders and restocking. WHY IT MATTERS: with spot below the quarterly benchmark, remaining Japanese buyers have little reason to settle above $255/t, and the Q1-2027 talks start from a lower spot base.

drivers.text: Chinese primary imports fell 14.65% year on year in August, which means less Chinese competition for ex-China metal — Public customs data reported on 25-September show China's August primary aluminium imports at 185,500 tonnes, DOWN 14.65% year on year and up just 0.16% month on month, with Russia supplying 178,150 tonnes or 96% of the total and Australia (2,920 t), Indonesia (2,180 t) and Malaysia (1,800 t) accounting for almost all of the remainder. Net imports were 163,600 tonnes, down 14.67% year on year. January-August imports were 1.66 million tonnes, down 3.41%. THE STATED CAUSE IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN DEMAND-LED: domestic capacity is at the 45-million-tonne policy ceiling, end-use demand from grid investment, electric vehicles and photovoltaic mounting is described as resilient, and inventory is being drawn down through semis exports rather than primary imports. WHY IT MATTERS FOR PREMIUMS EVEN SO: a premium is set by competition for units at a location. China importing 14.65% less primary metal, and 96% of what it does import arriving from a single discounted-origin supplier, means the marginal ex-China unit faces less Chinese competition - which works against premiums in Japan, Europe and the United States regardless of why Chinese buying fell.
drivers.source: AL Circle - China Aug aluminium imports down 14.7% year on year, Russia accounts for 96% of supply (25-September-2026)

drivers.text: Chinese semis exports hit a 2026 high, which pressures converter margins in exactly the markets where premiums are assessed — Public data reported on 25-September show China's August aluminium extrusion exports at 92,500 tonnes, the highest monthly figure of 2026, up 9.7% year on year from 84,300 tonnes and 3.0% month on month from 89,800 tonnes, taking January-August to 629,600 tonnes, up 8.7%. South-East Asia took 26,500 tonnes or 28.6% and was the only region with both the largest volume and double-digit growth; Africa took 18,800 tonnes and Latin America 14,400. SEPTEMBER IS GUIDED LOWER at 85,000-92,000 tonnes because the China-to-overseas price spread has narrowed, compressing margins on independent order-taking; the share of processing trade rose while ordinary trade fell, which the source reads as marginal weakening in price-driven independent orders. THE PREMIUM READ IS SPECIFIC: extrusions compete with locally converted metal in third markets. More Chinese semis arriving in South-East Asia, Africa and Latin America pressures the converter margins that ultimately support regional ingot premiums, even though the same exports support Chinese domestic ingot demand. The two effects are opposite and are stated separately rather than netted.
drivers.source: AL Circle - China's August aluminium extrusion exports hit a YTD high; pullback expected in September amid narrowing price spread (25-September-2026)

logistics.label: Strait of Hormuz transit
logistics.note: REVIEWED SATURDAY 10-OCTOBER-2026. Trading Economics' Brent coverage (09-October) says the US-Iran conflict continues to strain shipping: tankers are tied up in ship-to-ship transfers outside the Strait of Hormuz, freight rates are at record highs and eleven tankers were attacked in the Strait in the week ending 04-October; President Trump said the US would not strike Iran again before the midterm elections. No container or bulk transit count is published because tracker figures remain disputed. Arrow stays UP pending a public, verifiable normalisation signal. PRIOR: REVIEWED WEDNESDAY 30-SEPTEMBER-2026. Public reporting on 29-September records the US rejecting Iran's seven-day Hormuz reopening plan, new US sanctions on 10 suppliers to Iran's military, and Tehran awaiting a formal US response to its ceasefire proposal; the Strait remains closed. Middle East crude exports reached 12.8 million b/d, the highest since February, but largely via ship-to-ship transfers and pipeline bypasses that do not serve Gulf aluminium exports. No transit count is published because tracker figures remain disputed. Arrow stays UP. PRIOR: REVIEWED TUESDAY 29-SEPTEMBER-2026. Public reporting on 28-September records indirect US-Iran talks resuming through mediators in New York, with the Strait of Hormuz still closed to commercial shipping; Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline resumed after drone-strike repairs, with flows reported near 3.5 million b/d, offering a partial bypass for crude but not for Gulf aluminium exports. Transit counts remain disputed between trackers and outlets, so no transit figure is published. Arrow stays UP until a dated, verifiable reopening step. PRIOR: REVIEWED MONDAY 28-SEPTEMBER-2026. On Saturday 26-September the US President publicly rejected Iran's seven-day roadmap - release of frozen funds, lifting of oil sanctions and an end to the naval blockade within four to five days, with the Strait reopened and negotiations under way by day seven - calling it not acceptable. He told reporters he expects talks to resume in the coming week; separately, US officials were reported as signalling a renewed bombing campaign after the November midterms. Iran's foreign minister said Tehran will not back down on its conditions and awaits mediators' formal feedback. Public tracking (straits.live, 27-September) classifies the Strait as closed to commercial traffic on day 210, with a pre-crisis baseline of about 85 transits a day; some outlets report sizeable US-escorted crude movements, so transit counts are DISPUTED and none is used as a figure here. TREAT THESE AS REPORTED DIPLOMATIC STATEMENTS, NOT SETTLED OUTCOMES. WHY THE ARROW GOES FROM FLAT BACK TO UP: last week's cut to flat rested on a visible negotiation; its latest proposal was publicly rejected and a post-midterm escalation path was reported. Second-order effects stand: regional disruption withdraws tonnage from the global pool and reprices freight on lanes that never touch the Strait.

US forces disabled the cargo vessel Ocean Molica in the Gulf of Oman, the fourth commercial vessel disabled since the blockade of Iranian ports resumed on 14-July, alongside 135 ships turned around. backtest.verdict: These condition indicators showed NO predictive edge when tested: a 35.5% directional hit rate against a 67.9% naive 'always higher' baseline over the same sample, and forward returns after 'tightening' readings averaged 0.82% versus 6.81% after 'loosening' readings. They are therefore published as a read on CURRENT market condition only — not as a price forecast. The forward baseline and probability range above are the forward-looking view.
backtest.caveat: Measured on overlapping 13-week windows of weekly LME data (107 observations, 2024-05-24 to 2026-07-10). Overlapping windows overstate significance and the sample spans a single, largely rising market — evidence in either direction is weak.

THE WORLD'S LARGEST ALUMINA PRODUCER EARNED MATERIALLY LESS IN A QUARTER WHEN THE LME CASH AVERAGE WAS ABOVE $3,200, AND THAT IS THE SIGNAL. A 26% year-on-year fall in Q2 attributable profit on flat-to-lower revenue points to margin compression rather than volume weakness, and it is consistent with the Chinese alumina spot picture carried on this board - SMM's Shandong index down toward 2,600 RMB/t with national capacity utilisation rising and trader inventories building. For a reader of the seaborne market the implication runs both ways: weaker Chinese alumina margins are disinflationary for the smelter cost basket globally, but a large integrated producer earning less at a high metal price also argues that the cost curve has moved up underneath everyone. The shares fell around 3% on the release. earnings.note: STRONGEST QUARTER OF THE YEAR AT THE DOWNSTREAM END OF THE CHAIN. Fourth-quarter FY26 revenue rose 25.2% year-on-year to MYR 204.8 million (USD 50.8 million) from MYR 163.5 million (USD 40.5 million), on higher sales volumes in the group's extrusion and fabrication segment; the company reports its strongest quarterly revenue and profit of the financial year, with the headline putting quarterly profit up about 200% to roughly USD 4.5 million. The result funds a MYR 100 million (USD 24.8 million) expansion plan and a diversification away from its core solar-sector business. FIGURES ARE TAKEN FROM THE PUBLIC REPORT AS PUBLISHED; the full profit-and-loss detail below the revenue line was truncated in the public summary and nothing is inferred to fill it. A USEFUL COUNTERWEIGHT TO THE CHINESE DOWNSTREAM PICTURE RATHER THAN A CONTRADICTION OF IT, AND THE DISTINCTION IS GEOGRAPHIC. SMM's 24-August daily describes Chinese downstream processing operating rates as under pressure with pre-peak-season stockpiling absent, and Chinese billet inventory is at a five-year seasonal high. A South-East Asian extruder posting 25% revenue growth and its best quarter of the year says the weakness is not uniform across Asia - which is consistent with the trade-flow story on this board, where South-East Asia is being consolidated as the major supplementary scrap source by the UAE export ban and EU tariff increase. IT IS A SMALL COMPANY AND ONE QUARTER, SO IT IS WEIGHTED ACCORDINGLY: it is evidence that extrusion demand outside China is holding, not evidence that the global peak season has arrived.

earnings.note: H1-2026 interim results: alumina sales volume 1.296 Mt (+15.0% y/y from ~1.127 Mt) but average realised selling price USD 320/t against USD 529/t (-39.5%); revenue USD 415.0m (-30.5% y/y from USD 596.8m); gross profit USD 65.5m from USD 303.9m; gross margin 15.8% from 50.9%; profit attributable USD 62.7m (-74.8%); basic EPS USD 0.10 from USD 0.46; interim dividend cut to HKD 0.16 from HKD 0.65. Cash and equivalents more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings; total assets USD 2.496bn (+11.0%). THE VALUE OF THIS DISCLOSURE IS THAT IT IS A REALISED PRICE ACROSS 1.3 MILLION TONNES, NOT AN ASSESSMENT - which makes it the single best public measurement of how far alumina has actually fallen. A 39.5% decline in realised ASP to USD 320/t, against a company-stated average international alumina price of about USD 307/t on an LME Platts basis versus about USD 447/t a year earlier, confirms from the seller's own accounts that the 2024-25 alumina squeeze has fully unwound. FOR THE METAL THIS IS MARGIN-POSITIVE AND PRICE-NEGATIVE, AND BOTH LEGS DESERVE EQUAL BILLING: non-integrated smelters buy alumina cheaper, but a lower cost curve lowers the price at which supply discipline would ever appear. THE SECOND-ORDER POINT IS THE CAPITAL: cash more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings, funding preparatory work on a 250,000 t/y Indonesian electrolytic aluminium first phase at about USD 436.6m over roughly two years with a further 500,000 t/y flagged medium term. Weak alumina prices are not slowing the ex-China metal capacity pipeline - they are being converted into it. Public disclosure only; no company-specific or confidential information is used or implied.

earnings.readthrough: THE VALUE OF THIS DISCLOSURE IS THAT IT IS A REALISED PRICE ACROSS 1.3 MILLION TONNES, NOT AN ASSESSMENT - which makes it the single best public measurement of how far alumina has actually fallen. A 39.5% decline in realised ASP to USD 320/t, against a company-stated average international alumina price of about USD 307/t on an LME Platts basis versus about USD 447/t a year earlier, confirms from the seller's own accounts that the 2024-25 alumina squeeze has fully unwound. FOR THE METAL THIS IS MARGIN-POSITIVE AND PRICE-NEGATIVE, AND BOTH LEGS DESERVE EQUAL BILLING: non-integrated smelters buy alumina cheaper, but a lower cost curve lowers the price at which supply discipline would ever appear. THE SECOND-ORDER POINT IS THE CAPITAL: cash more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings, funding preparatory work on a 250,000 t/y Indonesian electrolytic aluminium first phase at about USD 436.6m over roughly two years with a further 500,000 t/y flagged medium term. Weak alumina prices are not slowing the ex-China metal capacity pipeline - they are being converted into it. Public disclosure only; no company-specific or confidential information is used or implied.

earnings.note: SWUNG BACK TO PROFIT ON THE PRICE CYCLE, WITH TEXTBOOK OPERATING LEVERAGE. Unaudited H1-2026 interim results, approved at an 18-August board meeting and filed 19-August: ADJUSTED EBITDA UP 64.4% TO US$1.23bn from US$748m; revenue up 10.9% to US$8.338bn from US$7.52bn; adjusted net profit US$196m against a US$194m loss a year earlier. REVENUE UP A TENTH AGAINST EBITDA UP NEARLY TWO-THIRDS IS THE SAME OPERATING-LEVERAGE SIGNATURE EVERY OTHER PRODUCER ON THIS PANEL HAS REPORTED FOR THE FIRST HALF, and it confirms the pattern extends beyond Western and Gulf smelters. The cost line is the part worth noting rather than the profit line: sales cost rose only 3.3% while revenue rose 10.9%, so the margin expansion came from price rather than from cost deflation, and the company specifically attributed what cost inflation there was to ENERGY. earnings.note: Revenue RMB 11.53bn, up 32.4% year on year. Net profit attributable to owners RMB 2.30bn, up 166.1%. EPS RMB 1.11 against RMB 0.58 in the corresponding period of last year, up 91.4%. THE CLEANEST PUBLIC READ THIS WEEK ON HOW FAR SMELTER MARGIN HAS EXPANDED AT 2026 PRICES, AND IT COMES FROM AN INTEGRATED, SELF-SUPPLIED PRODUCER. The company operates 788,100 t/y of electrolytic aluminium capacity in Huolinguole, Inner Mongolia with a captive power plant, plus an alumina refining and aluminium hydroxide base in Binzhou, Shandong; it states that self-sufficiency in alumina and electricity fully meets its production requirements. Profit attributable rose 166% on revenue up 32%, which is operating leverage of roughly five times and is only possible when the price rises against a cost base that does not. Management attributes the gain to higher electrolytic aluminium selling prices, lower production cost from a rising green-energy share, and an optimised financing structure. TWO FORWARD DISCLOSURES MATTER BEYOND the quarter: 1,040 MW of wind and 110 MW of solar were commissioned by end-June with the programme roughly 66% complete and the green share expected to exceed 50%, which lowers the cost base further; and the 500,000 t/y integrated electrolytic aluminium project in Saudi Arabia, invested with partners in 2025, had completed all compliance approvals with on-site construction in full swing. That project is a dated, sourced addition to the non-Chinese capacity pipeline. THE UNCOMFORTABLE IMPLICATION FOR PRICE BULLS: margins this wide at the low end of the cost curve are exactly the condition that funds new capacity, and this disclosure shows the funding and the capacity in the same document.

earnings.note: MARGINS EXPANDED SHARPLY WITH A THIRD OF THE VOLUME GONE. Adjusted net profit Dh2.46bn, up 34% year-on-year. Adjusted EBITDA Dh4.51bn, up 11% from Dh4.07bn, with the adjusted EBITDA margin widening to 33.3% from 27.0%. Revenue FELL 10% to Dh13.54bn from Dh15.08bn as aluminium sales dropped 32% to 939,000 t and cast metal production fell 29% to 1.01 Mt following the March incident at Al Taweelah. Reported net income Dh1.74bn after a Dh725m net incident impact. The company estimates around Dh1.5bn of capital expenditure to restore Al Taweelah, most of it in 2026, and guided cast metal back to pre-incident levels in Q1-2027 with the smelter at 25% of its reduction cells as of 26-Aug-2026 (315 of 1,262). THE COMPOSITION IS A PUBLIC CONFIRMATION OF THE MARGIN STRUCTURE THIS BOARD HAS DESCRIBED ALL CYCLE. Profit rose on three named drivers - higher realised aluminium prices, stronger regional premiums and LOWER ALUMINA PRICES - while a third of the sales volume was simply unavailable. A 630 basis-point margin expansion on a 10% revenue decline is only possible when the cost side has fallen faster than the top line, and the alumina leg is the reason. IT ALSO EXPLAINS TODAY'S PRICE ACTION IN ONE LINE: the same release that showed the margin also showed the recovery date, and the market traded the recovery date. The read-across to the alumina panel is direct - if Alunorte's 50% rate ends up lifting seaborne alumina, this is the margin that compresses first across the Gulf fleet.

earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

earnings.note: BACK-FILLED INTO THE PER-COMPANY HISTORY PANEL THIS RUN WITH FOUR SOURCED QUARTERS OF ADJUSTED EBITDA. Q1 FY27 (three months to 30-June-2026): net income $164m, up 71% year on year; ADJUSTED EBITDA $516m, UP 24% year on year; adjusted EBITDA per tonne shipped $563, up 30% year on year; net sales $5.8bn. The prior three quarters were $459m in Q4 FY26 (down 3% y/y, $544/t), $348m in Q3 FY26 (down 5% y/y, $430/t) and $422m in Q2 FY26 (down 9% y/y, $448/t) - all three depressed by the Oswego fires of September and November 2025 and by tariff headwinds. THE FOUR-QUARTER SERIES IS THE POINT AND IT IS WHY THIS COMPANY WAS CHOSEN FOR THIS RUN'S BACKFILL: it is the cleanest public evidence available of how a downstream converter recovers from an operational shock, and of what the 2026 premium environment has been worth to the downstream. Adjusted EBITDA fell for three consecutive quarters - $422m, $348m, $459m - and then stepped up 12.4% sequentially and 24% year on year to $516m in the June quarter. THE PER-TONNE LINE IS THE MORE INFORMATIVE OF THE TWO because it strips shipment volume out: $448, $430, $544, $563. That is a 31% improvement in unit conversion economics across four quarters in a business whose metal cost is passed through. WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE IS AS IMPORTANT AS WHAT IT DOES: a converter's EBITDA per tonne rising through a period of record US premiums is consistent with the premium being captured downstream, but Novelis does not publish a split between recovered metal-price spread, recycling spread and true conversion pricing, so this page does not claim one. Leverage was 1.8x at the quarter end. Management states that the 2028 targets of $900m ex-lag EBITDA and $300m of free cash flow will now be met two years early. THE METAL PRICE LAG IS THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS FOR READING THIS PAGE and it is disclosed by the company: the $439m headline INCLUDES a $129m non-cash benefit from metal price lag, so the ex-lag figure is $310m. The four-quarter ex-lag path is $196m, $213m, $262m, $310m against headline figures of $235m, $280m, $359m and $439m - the gap between the two series has widened every quarter. THE READ-THROUGH IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE ON THIS PANEL FOR ANYONE TRYING TO SIZE HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 EARNINGS CYCLE IS REAL. Constellium is a converter, not a smelter: it buys primary and scrap and sells rolled and extruded product, so a rising LME shows up in its results as a NON-CASH metal price lag benefit before it shows up anywhere in the operating business. That lag contributed $126m across the whole of FY2025 and $226m in the FIRST HALF of 2026 alone - it has nearly doubled in half the time. UNDERLYING PERFORMANCE IS GENUINELY GOOD, with ex-lag Adjusted EBITDA up 58% from $196m in Q3-2025 to $310m in Q2-2026 and the company pulling its 2028 targets forward by two years - but a reader who takes the $439m headline as operating performance overstates it by 29%. THE GENERAL POINT EXTENDS ACROSS THIS WHOLE PANEL: a large share of the 2026 aluminium earnings recovery is price-lag and inventory revaluation rather than volume or spread, which is exactly the kind of earnings that reverses when the LME stops rising - and the completed August board, on which aluminium's monthly mean rose 2.97% against copper's 6.12% and zinc's 7.76%, is the first evidence that it may be about to.

Kaiser reported record Q2-2026 adjusted EBITDA of $166.3m against $67.7m a year earlier, a 146% increase, on net sales of $1.2566bn and conversion revenue of $437.0m. GAAP net income was $96.8m or $5.72 per diluted share against $23.2m and $1.41. Adjusted EBITDA margin on conversion revenue doubled to 38.1% from 18.1%. H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA was $294.8m against $141.1m. Net debt leverage improved to 2.1x from 3.4x at 31-December-2025 and the full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook was raised to +45-55% year on year from +20-30%. Shipments rose 6% to 305.7 million lbs, led by packaging at 155.8 million lbs and aerospace/high-strength at 60.8 million. THE READ-THROUGH IS A WARNING ABOUT HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 DOWNSTREAM EARNINGS CYCLE IS A PRICE ARTEFACT RATHER THAN A DEMAND ONE, AND KAISER DISCLOSES IT MORE HONESTLY THAN MOST. Adjusted EBITDA includes management-estimated FAVOURABLE METAL PRICE LAG of approximately $27.0m in Q2-2026 and $36.0m in Q1-2026 - $64.0m across the half against $36.0m in H1-2025. That is roughly 22% of H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA arising from the timing difference between the Midwest Transaction Price embedded in cost of sales and the market price over the period, not from conversion economics. MANAGEMENT SAID SO EXPLICITLY: the raised full-year outlook 'assumes a NEUTRAL metal price lag through the end of the year, and does not assume a continuation of the metal lag or consumption cost tailwinds recorded in the first half', and the CEO said the company expects aluminium price dynamics to normalise over the balance of the year. THE COMMERCIAL LESSON FOR READING THIS WHOLE PANEL: a rising aluminium price inflates downstream converter earnings twice - once through genuine mix and volume, once through inventory timing - and the second half reverses if the price stops rising. Kaiser's underlying story is nevertheless real: conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.43 from $1.30, packaging conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.12 from $0.92, and aerospace shipments grew as destocking eased. Both things are true at once and the filing quantifies the split, which is why this row is worth its place.

The 118,000-tonne two-week destock to 24-September is attributed by its own source to pre-holiday stockpiling and a widening spot-futures spread. Both drivers reverse by design once the holiday ends: stockpiled metal is consumed rather than bought, and the spread normalises. If Chinese inventory rebuilds sharply in the first two weeks of October, the single strongest bullish number on this page will have been a calendar effect; if it does not rebuild, the destock was demand and the deficit case strengthens materially. THE CHINESE DOWNSTREAM OVERHANG IS HELD AT UP AND THE EVIDENCE GOT BROADER RATHER THAN DEEPER. SMM's 24-September South China review records transactions concentrated at a 250-290 yuan/tonne premium over the SHFE 2610 contract but quotes lowered repeatedly through the session, most deals concluded at actual DISCOUNTS, phased stockpiling complete, procurement slowing and spot circulation shifting to oversupply, with cashing out before the holiday the dominant driver. To that this run adds a structural leg: August extrusion exports at a 2026 high of 92,500 tonnes with September guided lower on a narrowing China-to-overseas price spread that compresses exporter margins, and processing trade gaining share over ordinary trade. A physical market clearing at discounts while exporting record volumes on thinning margins is a demand picture that depends on price, not on need. THE COST FLOOR IS CUT FROM UP TO DOWN, AND IT IS THE MOST ECONOMICALLY MEANINGFUL MACRO MOVE ON THE BOARD TODAY. European gas TTF fell 4.02% to EUR 71.93/MWh on the 25-September reference session, the largest single-session fall of this window, and Brent slipped 0.56% to $106.01 after the previous session's 3.90% jump. Power is roughly 30-40% of smelter cash cost and is the largest single line after alumina, so a falling energy complex lowers the marginal cost floor and therefore the price floor. IT ALSO WORKS THE OTHER WAY AND BOTH ARE STATED: cheaper European gas directly improves the economics of the European smelting capacity publicly guided to return, which is a supply risk rather than a price support. The arrow is down because the floor fell; the supply consequence is carried on the ex-China restart row. STRAIT OF HORMUZ AND REGIONAL SHIPPING DISRUPTION IS RAISED FROM FLAT TO UP, BECAUSE THE ONE THING THAT HAD IMPROVED - THE DIPLOMATIC TRACK - WENT BACKWARDS OVER THE WEEKEND. EU CARBON-BORDER COST IS A SLOW, STRUCTURAL RISK TO EUROPEAN DELIVERED PRICE AND IT IS HELD AT FLAT. No new dated instrument or rate change printed into this window. The 6% EU import duty plus the carbon border adjustment mechanism remains a structural floor under European delivered prices and a persistent disadvantage for high-carbon origins, which is why the European duty-unpaid premium and the Rotterdam duty-paid billet premium behave differently from the Japanese benchmark. It is carried here as a structural risk rather than a live one precisely because it moves on legislative rather than market timescales.

balance.label: UPDATE 02-OCTOBER: Macquarie revised its 2026 deficit to 820,000 t from 940,000 t and forecasts a 410,000 t surplus in 2027, citing the faster EGA Al Taweelah restart (via Discovery Alert). Deficit - Goldman -720 kt, Norsk Hydro -900 kt, Macquarie -930 kt; Citi an outlier at -2.7 Mt. THE BALANCE VIEW IS UNCHANGED AND THE 11-SEPTEMBER DATA SHARPENS THE CENTRAL PUZZLE RATHER THAN RESOLVING IT: global primary production was reported down 1.7% year on year at 6.16 million tonnes and GCC output down 44% year on year in July to 293,000 tonnes from 523,000 - a genuine, large supply loss. YET China's August exports were 626,000 tonnes, taking January-August to 4.67 million tonnes, up 16.7% year on year, and dated commentary describes Middle Eastern and Australian ingot supply into Japan as RELATIVELY AMPLE with Asian premiums collapsing toward a $280-290 Q4 consensus. A DEFICIT IN PRIMARY UNITS CAN COEXIST WITH AMPLE REGIONAL AVAILABILITY IF THE RELIEVING METAL ARRIVES AS CHINESE SEMI-FINISHED AND ALLOY PRODUCT THAT NEVER PASSES THROUGH AN LME WAREHOUSE - which is the most coherent published explanation for why a multi-decade exchange inventory low, a widening backwardation and collapsing physical premiums are all true at once.

The published restart schedule is the reason, and it gained another dated entry on 20-August. Nanshan Aluminum's 2026 semi-annual report confirms 250,000 t/y of Indonesian aluminium and 260,000 t/y of carbon under construction at Bintan Industrial Park, with the integrated anode carbon removing one of the genuine physical constraints on commissioning new non-Chinese capacity. Alongside it: Gulf pre-incident output guided for Q1-2027 and running faster than the market expected; Slovalco 75,000 t/y from Q4-2026; Magnitude 7 Metals 75,000 t/y before year-end; Mount Holly already at full capacity and lifting US primary output by close to 10%; the Australian smelter's power secured to 2038 removing a closure risk over up to 590,000 t/y; Alunorte back at full rate; and a 500,000 t/y integrated Saudi greenfield through all compliance approvals with construction under way. These are published commitments with dates attached rather than projections, which is why the deficit is expected to narrow rather than persist at 2026 scale.
